authority.scope: Generic L6 file-backed index synchronization only; no app identity, semantic policy, threshold, route, provider, or Exit behavior.
authority.reason: Independent adversarial review proved repair-only compare-and-swap could not prevent stale preinitialized writers or same-instance readers from erasing recovered or concurrent bindings.

design_invariants: Version and trace index writers share one bounded cross-process OS lock with recovery tooling.
Every durable writer reloads and validates the current mapping and persists an operation-local merged mapping under the lock.
Canonical index paths remain present during atomic replacement; recovery never renames them into a missing-path claim window.
Process exit releases the persistent sidecar lock without stale-file cleanup or split-lock recreation.
The mechanism is app-neutral and remains inside L6 system-learning storage.

negative_controls: Two preinitialized spawned version writers preserve both mappings.
A live version writer waits behind version-index recovery and merges the complete recovered map.
A live runtime writer waits behind trace recovery and preserves recovered plus new trace/snapshot bindings.
Same-instance readers cannot reset operation-local writer maps before save.
Lock contention times out, non-finite timeouts are rejected, and crash/process exit releases the lock.
Archive mismatch preflight with a missing version index causes no version or trace publication.
Ambiguous trace authority remains unresolved and is receipted without fabricated binding.
Trace-less snapshots retain recoverable snapshot-ID aliases.
Integer nanosecond freshness comparison rejects pre-spawn generation manifests without float-rounding authorization on Windows.
